title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
why_read: A robotics safety paper addressing a real gap: knowing whether an action is dangerous depends on who or what it is being performed on.
analysis: This paper tackles the problem that AI-generated motion for humanoid robots can be ambiguous in safety terms, since the same gesture might be safe towards an object but dangerous towards a person. The authors propose a training-free filtering system that uses example safe and unsafe trajectories to build a mathematical safety boundary, enforced through a control technique called a control barrier function. They tested it on a real humanoid robot (Unitree G1) and report it cuts dangerous events by up to 90% while mostly preserving normal behavior. This is a meaningful contribution to practical robot safety, especially as humanoid robots increasingly interact with people in shared spaces.
